name: Tomás Pablo Korenblit
summary: Finishing a BSc in Data Science focused on Bayesian inference. I build hierarchical Bayesian models of how LLM behavior degrades. My recent work shows that aggregate compliance metrics hide large per-instruction failures, and that stating a preference a model already follows can make it comply less.

bullets: Studying LLM threat models. Extending the PowerBench work
Facilitating BlueDot's Technical AI Safety course, and taking their Projects course
Built a graph of investors, founders, and companies across the Americas, MENA, and Europe, with warm-intro pathfinding and community detection over it
Wrote an assistant to turn English into Cypher, so non-technical users can query the graph directly (Python, Neo4j, PostgreSQL, FastAPI, GCP)
Designed a RAG platform to create almost all RLHF annotation interfaces
Wrote validation tools and dashboards (Python, Looker) used company-wide. Reviewed output quality for the LLM training teams
Made a lead generation system and trained a classifier on client profiles to qualify them (Python, Pandas, PostgreSQL, Scikit-learn)

publications.title: Not All Instructions Are Forgotten Equal
bullets: Aggregate compliance hides per-instruction failures. Per-instruction treatment effects span more than an order of magnitude, so a model can drop a stated preference while mean compliance stays high
Stating a preference a model already follows can backfire. Told not to add new imports, models added more. Explicit negation seems to push the model off a good default
Hierarchical Bayesian ordered-logistic model fit in PyMC. Scored with deterministic checkers, no LLM in the loop

publications.title: PowerBench: LLM Refusal in Power-Grabbing Requests
publications.venue: Apart Research Global South AI Safety Hackathon
bullets: Adding self-benefit to a harmful request lowers refusal. Models refuse pure disempowerment (harm to others) more than power-grabbing (harm plus self-gain). Holds across five models
Refusal of these requests does not correlate with model capability, so it reflects training choices
Multilingual, single-turn first-person requests, scored by an LLM judge not yet validated against human labels
